c.tagline: Argentina's self-declared 'Trekking Capital,' a tiny village beneath the jagged spires of Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre

card: Accepted at larger hotels; cash preferred at small guesthouses and shops

taxi.fareNote: The village is tiny and walkable; taxis are mainly for arriving/departing bus and airport transfers

emergency.note: 911 is the general emergency line in most of Argentina; medical facilities in the village are basic

walk: The village itself is tiny and entirely walkable; the famous treks to Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre begin right from town on marked trails

safety.safety: Very safe village, though mountain weather is notoriously unpredictable and changes quickly
safety.crime: Minimal crime; the main risk is weather and trail conditions for trekkers

hood_landmark.Village Center: El Chaltén's small main street of outfitters and restaurants
hood_landmark.Laguna de los Tres Trailhead: The trailhead for the classic Fitz Roy viewpoint trek
hood_landmark.Laguna Torre Trailhead: The trailhead for the Cerro Torre viewpoint trek
hood_landmark.Chorrillo del Salto: The easy Chorrillo del Salto waterfall walk
hood_landmark.Los Glaciares National Park Entrance: The Los Glaciares National Park visitor center

hood_desc: The tiny village core with most guesthouses, restaurants, and outdoor outfitters; the entire town is walkable in minutes.
The starting point (right from town) for the classic full-day trek to the iconic Fitz Roy viewpoint at Laguna de los Tres.
The starting point for the trek to Laguna Torre, offering views of the equally dramatic (and often cloud-wrapped) Cerro Torre spire.
A short, easy walk from town to a scenic waterfall, good for a half-day outing or rest-day activity.
The park visitor center at the entrance to Los Glaciares National Park, where trekking permits and trail conditions are available.

water.note: Glacier-fed tap water is safe to drink.

transit.sys: No formal transit; the village is tiny and walkable
transit.map: Not applicable given the village's small size
transit.note: El Chaltén has no ATM reliability guarantee; bring sufficient cash from El Calafate

transport.air: El Calafate Airport (FTE), about 3 hr away by road, is the nearest airport
transport.bus: Daily buses connect to El Calafate (about 3 hr)
transport.car: Reachable via National Route 40 and Provincial Route 23; a rental car offers flexibility for the scenic drive

airport.name: El Calafate Airport (nearest gateway)
airport.transport: Bus or rental car from El Calafate

net.m: Limited 3G/4G coverage in the village, none on the trails
net.w: Wifi available in some hotels but often slow
net.fwn: Wifi available in central guesthouses, though unreliable
net.ap: A Movistar, Claro, or Personal tourist SIM or eSIM
